derived: Worked out by hand from excerpts/app/models/concerns/heartbeatable.rb and excerpts/lib/wakatime_service.rb. WP-PG0 did not run them; WP-PG11 runs every case through durations.sql on Postgres. A mismatch there means the SQL, these numbers or the Ruby reading is wrong, and the Ruby decides.

sets.name: two projects, a boundary heartbeat, an excluded category, a NULL category, a deleted row and another user's row

cases.name: test mode total: the gap from the boundary heartbeat counts, and long gaps are capped at 120 s
cases.why: Ids 7 (browsing), 9 (no category), 11 (deleted) and 12 (another user) drop out. The boundary is id 2 at 950. Gaps ending in the window: 80, 30, 30, 30, then 310 and 570, each capped at 120.

cases.name: no_ai_coding=true leaves the ai coding heartbeat out of the timeline
cases.why: Without id 8 the gaps are 80, 30, 30, 30 and 880 capped at 120.

cases.name: the boundary heartbeat is the last one of the filtered projects, not the last one overall
cases.why: Only project a: the boundary is id 1 at 900, then 130 capped at 120, 60, 340 capped at 120 and 570 capped at 120.

cases.name: with no heartbeat before the window, the first one adds nothing
cases.why: No row before 800, so the window is 800 <= time <= 2000. Id 1 adds 0, then 50, 80, 30, 30, 30, 120 and 120.

cases.name: the plain sum stops before the window's end and has no boundary heartbeat
cases.why: 1000 <= time < 2000 keeps ids 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8. Id 10 at exactly 2000 is out. Id 3 adds 0, then 30, 30, 30 and 310 capped at 120.

cases.name: with no exclusion list, browsing and NULL categories count
cases.why: Ids 3 to 9 without 10 or 11: 0, 30, 30, 30, 280 capped at 120, 30 and 30.

cases.name: per-project gaps are taken inside each project, so the parts can exceed the whole
cases.why: a has 1030, 1090 and 1430, so 60 plus 340 capped at 120. b has 1060 and 1120, so 60. That is 240 against 210 for the same heartbeats in one order.

cases.name: each gap goes to the category of the heartbeat that ends it
cases.why: In one order the three 30 s gaps end on coding heartbeats and the capped 310 s gap ends on id 8. 90 plus 120 is the plain sum, 210.

cases.name: the category breakdown drops the NULL bucket
cases.why: The 280 s gap capped at 120 ends on id 7, browsing. Id 8 gets 30. Id 9's 30 s has no category and is dropped, so the buckets add up to 240, not the 270 of the plain sum.

cases.name: the integer cast rounds the sum instead of truncating it
cases.why: Two gaps of 0.8 s make 1.6 s, and ::integer rounds that to 2. Truncating would give 1.
